title: I Applied the Curling-Club Stone Handle Log to the Skip Who Took Our Numbered Pair

parts.text: I stepped into sheet two at 7:03 p.m. and skip Maren was already using numbered stone handles. The board said: ONE SHEET. TWO HOURS. HANDLES STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-one, league secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our draw. Maren shrugged. "Skips are the ice." I photographed the board, the booking, and her takeout on our hog line. Then I asked for the handle log. At 7:11 the ice desk pinged why Maren's name was on our pair. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The ice desk can see Maren's takeout on sheet two during our draw.

social.video_title: She took our numbered handles on our sheet — Part 1/2
social.description: Curling sheet, a skip on our hog line, a two-hour clock she posted. I logged the takeout. Would you have asked for the handle log?

parts.text: Maren called it practice slides until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the hog-line still. The handles went back to our numbered stones. Maren ran a slot of their own and told the next skip atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: SKIPS ARE NOT THE ICE. I keep our pair on a labeled rack. Maren brown-bags her jokes. The sheet finally looks like a draw, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Skips are not the ice — Part 2/2
social.description: Handle log, numbered pair, and a second line on the board. Was a practice slide ever our hog line?
